target_customer: Startups raising small amounts from many investors, and everyday (including non-accredited) investors
problem: Only accredited investors could buy startup equity; JOBS Act (2012) was expected to let anyone invest small amounts.

founders.name: Mike Norman
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on Wikipedia only (citation needed)

technical_complexity.rationale: Web platform with legal/escrow workflow; regulation more than technology was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Registration as funding portal and investor/startup two-sided network are hard to replicate quickly; not evidenced with sources read.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wikipedia navigation lists these as crowdfunding platforms; dated 2012-13 competitor evidence not gathered.

market_need_then: 2012 JOBS Act opened equity crowdfunding to non-accredited investors (Wikipedia); Reg CF rules did not take effect until 2016 (not sourced here).

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a plain compound and the tagline 'Everyone can invest $100' is clear; no external brand sources read.

outcome_analysis: Wefunder, YC W13, is listed Active at Growth stage with about 35 people. It rode the JOBS Act regulatory shift, which is the likely tailwind, but no funding, volume or competitor-outcome data was retrieved, so the strength of its success cannot be quantified here.
notes: Wikipedia says founded 2012 (citation needed) while the infobox and YC page say 2011. wefunder.com/about returned 403 and Crunchbase returned 403; not worked around. Funding for Wefunder itself not found. Research limit: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before any outcome, funding, competitor or branding search could run, so only the YC page and company site were read; competition_at_founding is left empty (no dated sources), and funding and brand origin facts are unverified or null.
